new.title: Step inside Paderborn Cathedral and its crypt
new.desc: The cathedral grew from a church attached to Charlemagne's palace of 777; Bishop Meinwerk's rebuilt cathedral was consecrated in 1015 and the Gothic hall church followed in the 13th century. Bombing in 1945 destroyed its old glass and reconstruction ran through the 1950s.
new.tip: Free to enter outside services; look for the crypt with the shrine of St Liborius.
new.q: Hoher Dom zu Paderborn, Domplatz, Paderborn

new.title: Spot the Three Hares window in the cathedral cloister
new.desc: The Dreihasenfenster, carved in red Weser sandstone in the early 16th century, shows three running hares sharing three ears. The original sits on the north side of the cloister courtyard, and copies decorate shops across the city centre.
new.tip: Find the cloister entrance on the north side of the cathedral; the original window is described as shown at the diocesan museum, so ask on site.

new.title: Watch Germany's strongest springs form the Pader
new.desc: Around 200 karst springs rise in the city, the strongest spring area in Germany, feeding the Pader, which is only about 4 km long and counts as Germany's shortest river. The main springs bubble from walled basins such as the Warme Pader and Dielenpader.
new.tip: Walk the paths beside the Paderquellgebiet right behind the cathedral; free at any time.

new.title: Explore Charlemagne's Kaiserpfalz and its museum
new.desc: Charlemagne built a palace here in 776; the Ottonian-Salian main hall was reconstructed after excavations from 1963 to 1978 and houses the LWL-Museum in der Kaiserpfalz since 1978. The nearby Bartholomew chapel is the only fully preserved Ottonian building of the complex.
new.tip: Closed on some Mondays; check the LWL site for hours.
new.q: LWL-Museum in der Kaiserpfalz, Am Ikenberg 1, Paderborn

new.title: Visit the Abdinghof church above the Pader
new.desc: The Benedictine abbey of Saints Peter and Paul dates to the 11th century and was dissolved in 1803. Rebuilt after the Second World War, the church is now the main Lutheran church of Paderborn, with a 1961 tracker organ of 34 stops.
new.tip: Open for visitors and organ concerts; the interior was renovated from 2023 to 2025.

new.title: Trace 5,000 years of computing at the Nixdorf MuseumsForum
new.desc: Housed in the former Nixdorf Computer headquarters, the museum opened in 1996 and presents 5,000 years of information technology from writing to robotics. It spreads across two floors with over 5,000 objects.
new.tip: Allow two to three hours; good for rainy days.

new.title: Join the nine-day Libori festival in July
new.desc: Libori is one of the largest and oldest folk festivals in Germany, tracing back to relics of St Liborius brought from Le Mans in 836. It mixes church processions with a 1.6 km fairground on the Liboriberg and ends with fireworks over the Pader springs.
new.tip: It starts on the first Saturday after 23 July; book hotels early.

new.title: Walk the Pader from its springs downstream
new.desc: The Pader flows only about 4 km from the springs behind the cathedral before joining the Lippe, passing through the old town and the green Paderaue. The springs discharge about 5,000 litres per second on average.
new.tip: Start at the springs and follow the river west; it is flat and free.

new.title: Take cake and quiche at Ostermann am Museum
new.desc: A bistro-cafe on Markt right next to the cathedral and the diocesan museum, listed by the tourist office for its savoury quiches, butter waffles, cakes and tarts made in-house.
new.tip: Try a Butterwaffel with coffee; a handy stop after the cathedral.
new.q: Bistro-Cafe Ostermann am Museum, Markt 17, Paderborn

new.title: Linger over coffee and cake at Markt 5 Cafe
new.desc: A cafe on Paderborn's market square, praised by guests for its cakes, coffee and calm atmosphere away from the busiest streets.
new.tip: Card payment only at the counter per reviews; ask for the cake of the day.

new.title: Drink Paderborner beer at Deutsches Haus on the Kisau
new.desc: A traditional restaurant with about 100 seats indoors and a beer garden, on the Kisau pub street. The Paderborner brewery, founded in 1852, is part of the local tradition and Paderborn has historically brewed mostly Pilsner.
new.tip: Order a Paderborner Pilsener with a regional main course; the brewery itself is listed for sale, so check what is on tap.

new.title: Sip specialty coffee at Deppe & Co
new.desc: A roaster that serves ethically sourced specialty coffee in its cafes in Bielefeld and Paderborn, listed by the Teutoburger Wald tourist board.
new.tip: Order the house espresso or a filter coffee of the day.

new.title: Tour Wewelsburg castle and its SS memorial
new.desc: A triangular Renaissance castle built 1603 to 1609 for the prince-bishops of Paderborn. The SS used it from 1934 and planned a cult centre; today it houses a history museum and the Wewelsburg 1933-1945 Memorial Museum.
new.tip: Allow half a day for both museums; closed on some Mondays.

new.title: Climb to the Hermannsdenkmal above Detmold
new.desc: The 53 m copper statue of Arminius by Ernst von Bandel stands on the Grotenburg, built 1838 to 1875 to commemorate the victory over Roman legions in 9 AD. It draws over 500,000 visitors a year.
new.tip: Climb the stairs inside the pedestal to the viewing gallery; park at the Hermannsdenkmal car park.

new.title: See the Externsteine rock towers and carved relief
new.desc: Thirteen sandstone pillars rise to 37.5 m in the Teutoburg Forest; the 12th-century relief of the Descent from the Cross on Rock I is the oldest monumental rock relief north of the Alps.
new.tip: Come early to avoid crowds; the rocks can be climbed by stairs.

new.title: Tour the Weser Renaissance Residenzschloss in Detmold
new.desc: First mentioned in 1366, rebuilt from 1549 as a four-wing Renaissance castle and given Baroque touches in 1715. Visitors can see the King's Rooms and the Ahnensaal; the castle is open daily except Mondays.
new.tip: Guided tours run at weekends.

new.title: Visit the Lippisches Landesmuseum, OWL's oldest museum
new.desc: Founded in 1835 as a natural history museum, it is described as the largest and oldest museum in Ostwestfalen-Lippe, with collections from prehistory to art and furniture, opposite Detmold castle.
new.tip: Combine with the castle across the street.

new.title: Admire the Hexenbürgermeisterhaus in Lemgo
new.desc: A Weser Renaissance merchant house built 1568 to 1571, named after mayor Hermann Cothmann, linked to the Lemgo witch trials. Its museum opened in 1926 and covers the house and Lemgo history.
new.tip: Note the Utlucht bay on the facade.

new.title: Marvel at the carved Junkerhaus in Lemgo
new.desc: A two-storey half-timbered house completed in 1891 by the painter and eccentric Karl Junker, who lived there until 1912 and covered it with carvings. Lemgo has maintained it since 1962 and restored it in 2004.
new.tip: Open as a museum; check museen-lemgo.de for times.

new.title: Walk into Minden Cathedral
new.desc: Construction started in 803 after Charlemagne conquered the area; the Romanesque westwork and Gothic hall survived until bombing in March 1945. Werner March rebuilt it in the 1950s.
new.tip: Free entry; combine with the Domschatz and Minden old town.

new.title: Watch ships cross the Weser at the Wasserstraßenkreuz
new.desc: At Minden the Mittelland Canal crosses the Weser in a 398 m trough bridge opened in 1998 beside the 1914 original, with a shaft lock lifting boats 13 m. It is one of Europe's biggest waterway junctions.
new.tip: Walk the canal path across the old and new bridges; a free spectacle.

new.title: Climb to the Kaiser Wilhelm Monument at Porta Westfalica
new.desc: An imposing monument about 88 m tall on the Wittekindsberg, honouring Kaiser Wilhelm I above the Weser gap known as the Westphalian Gate. It stands at about 268 m altitude and is run by the LWL.
new.tip: Reached by a short climb from the car park; public tours run.

new.title: See the moated Schloss Petershagen on the Weser
new.desc: A former moated castle of the Minden prince-bishops built around 1306 and converted to Weser Renaissance style in 1544 to 1547. Hotel operations ended in 2018; new owners from 2022 plan events.
new.tip: Check opening for events or tours before you go; grounds can be seen from outside.

new.title: Look at Burg Blomberg, a Lippe castle
new.desc: A 13th-century castle later remodelled in Weser Renaissance style from 1560 with a sandstone bay by Hermann Wulff. It was sold to the city in 1962 and has been privately owned since 2021.
new.tip: Hotel and restaurant use ended in 2019; check what is open before visiting.

new.title: Visit the Lippe spring and castle ruin in Bad Lippspringe
new.desc: The source of the river Lippe lies next to the ruin of a 13th/14th-century castle abandoned in 1785, and has a feature called Odin's Eye. The town takes its name from it.
new.tip: Free; combine with the Arminiuspark next door.

new.title: Admire the Wasserschloss in Schloss Neuhaus
new.desc: A Weser Renaissance moated castle in the Paderborn district at Schloss Neuhaus, a short bus ride from the city, on the Lippe and Pader. Listed here as a sight to visit with the Pader cafe nearby.
new.tip: Walk the castle gardens; free to enter the park.

new.title: Have rhubarb cake at Pader-Cafe in Schloss Neuhaus
new.desc: A cafe on Fürstenallee in Schloss Neuhaus, outside the Paderborn old town, with a visitor review praising its rhubarb cake.
new.tip: Go on a weekend afternoon; portions can vary.

new.title: Order Lippischer Pickert at Liebharts Sudhaus in Detmold
new.desc: A brewpub in Detmold whose menu lists Lippischer Pickert, a regional potato bread served with fresh butter, home-made liverwurst and plum jam.
new.tip: Try the Pickert as a light meal with house beer; confirm the current menu.
new.q: Liebharts Sudhaus Gasthausbrauerei, Am Gelskamp 15a, Detmold

new.title: Eat stew and Flammkuchen at Alte Remise in Lemgo
new.desc: A cafe at Breite Straße 10a next to the Abteigarten with a beer garden, serving home-made stews, soups and Flammkuchen alongside coffee and tea.
new.tip: Beer garden seating cannot be reserved; the cafe can.

new.title: Take a seasonal lunch at Cafe Vielfalt in Lemgo
new.desc: A cafe in a restored half-timbered building on Mittelstraße with fresh regional and seasonal food and a cultural programme.
new.tip: Check the events calendar for evening concerts.

new.title: Eat hearty German dishes at Beim Ritter in Bad Salzuflen
new.desc: A traditional German restaurant at Parkstraße 20 serving hearty home-style dishes near the Kurpark.
new.tip: Good after a Kurpark walk; ask for the daily regional special.

new.title: Dine on regional dishes at Zur Mühlenwirtin
new.desc: A thatched half-timbered farm in Grossenheerse near Petershagen with a restaurant, cafe and stork museum, serving regional specialities on the Westphalian mill route.
new.tip: Combine with a visit to nearby mills.
new.q: Landgasthaus Zur Mühlenwirtin, Großenheerser Mühle 4, Petershagen

new.title: Eat German home cooking at Gasthof Bad Hopfenberg
new.desc: A cafe, Gasthof and beer garden at Bremer Straße 26 in Petershagen serving classic German cooking near the Pottmühle on the mill route.
new.tip: Good stop on a cycling tour of the mill route.
new.q: Gasthof Bad Hopfenberg, Bremer Straße 26, Petershagen

new.title: Dine by the Weser at the Schiffmühlen Gastronomie in Minden
new.desc: A restaurant and beer garden at Weserpromenade 24 beside the reconstructed barge mill, serving German home-style and regional food.
new.tip: Sit outside in summer for river views.

new.title: Try potato dishes at Die Knolle im Pottkieker in Minden
new.desc: A rustic potato-themed restaurant at Königswall 1 in Minden, described as a Kartoffelhaus.
new.tip: Order a potato-based main; check the menu before booking.
new.q: Die Knolle im Pottkieker, Königswall 1, Minden

new.title: Wander the LWL open-air museum in Detmold
new.desc: One of Germany's largest open-air museums, decided in 1960, opened in 1971 and covering 90 hectares with about 120 historic buildings from across Westphalia.
new.tip: Plan a full day; closed in winter months.

new.title: Watch free-flight shows at Adlerwarte Berlebeck
new.desc: A raptor park opened at Pentecost 1939 with about 46 species and over 200 birds, with flight demonstrations several times a day and a rescue station since 1975.
new.tip: Arrive for the first flight show; seasonal.

new.title: Meet pelicans and toucans at Vogelpark Heiligenkirchen
new.desc: A 3.8 ha family-run park founded in 1969 with about 300 species and 1,000 animals, mostly exotic birds, plus kangaroos and marmosets.
new.tip: Good for families; allow two to three hours.

new.title: Breathe salt air at the Bad Salzuflen graduation works
new.desc: The graduation works, once 424 m long and now about 300 m, trickle brine to enrich the air. The Kurpark from 1907 along the Salze has a lake with fountain and boat hire.
new.tip: Walk the Gradierwerk then the Kurpark; entrance to the park is free.

new.title: Stroll Arminiuspark and the planet trail in Bad Lippspringe
new.desc: An English landscape park laid out in the 1840s with the Prinzenpalais and the Nebelwiese mist meadow, starting point of a 6 km scale-model Planetenweg.
new.tip: Combine with the Lippe spring.

new.title: Walk or sail around the Schiedersee
new.desc: A reservoir in the Emmer valley about 3.1 km long, finished in the early 1980s, with lifeguards, sailing and rowing clubs and a scheduled motor ship.
new.tip: Best in summer; shallow water.

new.title: Tour working windmills on German Mill Day
new.desc: The Westphalian Mill Route has 43 restored mills; almost all offer guided tours on Whit Monday (Deutscher Mühlentag) and on the fourth Sunday of August.
new.tip: Most mills open on milling and baking days, March to October.

new.title: Visit the 1748 Königsmühle windmill at Eilhausen
new.desc: A windmill built in 1748 at Eilhausen near Lübbecke, part of the Westphalian Mill Route.
new.tip: Open on milling days and Mill Day only.

new.title: See the Schönen-Mühle watermill at Bergkirchen
new.desc: A watermill at Bergkirchen in Bad Oeynhausen area on the Westphalian Mill Route, which includes nine watermills.
new.tip: Open on milling days.

new.title: Visit the 1883 Struckhof windmill in Hüllhorst
new.desc: A Dutch-style windmill built in 1883 in Hüllhorst, on the Westphalian Mill Route.
new.tip: Open on milling days.
